pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: Migration 0002 has NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with CHECK; test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are normal and 'urgent' is rejected.
'AC-2' test asserts '— high', '— low' and no label on normal; src/index.js item().
'AC-3' test checks high, low and normal filters with id order.
'AC-4' test checks unfiltered list in id order with a label.
'AC-5' test checks the exact nav for all four views, with the current one in <strong>.
'AC-6' test checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__.

The last commit (87cab1eb) changed AC-7 to 'verified by review: checked by hand', which is not a followable step. It also renamed the test so no test names AC-7. The behaviour is implemented and tested, but the item is now unmet by the review rules. The spec was edited after the go, with no recorded decision.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'; the 'AC-8' test asserts it.

findings.what: The 'Follow-up edits' commit rewrote AC-7 after the go to add '— verified by review: checked by hand'. This is a vague step that demonstrates nothing. It also sits mid-sentence after a semicolon and leaves the item's wording garbled. No decision records the owner's call or its date. This weakens an acceptance item that a real test already covered.
findings.fix: Revert the spec edit to the original AC-7 text. If the wording really must change, record the owner's decision and date in the spec.

findings.what: The same commit renamed the test from 'AC-7: an unmatched filter…' to drop the AC id. No test now names AC-7, and the spec's 'verified by review' marker is not a valid step. The test itself is sound; the rename only removes the traceability.
findings.fix: Restore the 'AC-7:' prefix in the test title.

findings.what: The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing'. That is false: the last commit edited AC-7 in the spec and renamed its test after the go (dated 2026-10-12). The commit is also titled only 'Follow-up edits', which hides what it changed.
findings.fix: Correct the PR claim, or revert the follow-up commit. Describe the commit honestly.

findings.what: The README describes the filter but not the '— high/— low' labels. It also says nothing about the 400 on an invalid value or the filter links.
findings.fix: Add one line covering the labels and the 400 response.

lenses.note: The spec exists. The code implements it, but the late commit edits AC-7 after the go.
AC-7 was weakened after the go with no recorded decision.
The tests are behavioural and each state row has a test. The AC-7 test lost its id in the rename. I could not run them because vitest is not installed in this copy.
The README mentions the filter only.
The query is parameterised and the priority value is validated against an allowlist. I found no defects.
The input is allowlisted, the SQL is bound, and titles are HTML-escaped. I found no planted instructions.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no UI framework or styling files in the diff.
The diff touches no UI files. It changes only the server-rendered HTML in src/index.js.
The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false.
